name: Alabama

notes: Food (what SNAP can buy, candy and soft drinks included) is taxed at a reduced 2% state rate since September 1, 2025 (Act 2025-305), plus local taxes at each city's and county's own grocery rate, which some set lower than their general rate. The state's 2% was suspended from May 1 to June 30, 2026 (Act 2026-604); the current 2% is used here.

Alcohol is taxed at the full rate, on top of excise taxes and, for liquor, the state ABC Board's markup, which are left out here. Oxford's higher city rate on alcohol is counted there, and Jefferson County's 3% on beer and liquor and 6% alcoholic beverage tax on liquor are counted on drinks served there (in its cities too); Columbiana's added 4% on liquor and wine is noted on its page.

Cigarettes and other tobacco are taxed at the full rate, on top of excise taxes left out here: 67.5 cents a pack of cigarettes, 34 cents a pack of heated tobacco and 10 cents a milliliter of vapor liquid, plus many cities' and counties' own per-pack taxes.

Personal care products: diapers, baby wipes and menstrual products are exempt from the state tax from September 1, 2025 to August 31, 2028 (Act 2025-304), and from local taxes only where a city or county opted in; that isn't taken out here.
Barber and beauty services, laundry and dry cleaning, and auto repair labor: not taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).

Clothing is taxed. The back-to-school sales tax holiday (July 17 to 19, 2026) exempted clothing of $156 or less an item, school supplies and computers from the state tax and from local taxes where they took part, which is not taken out here.
Motor fuel is exempt from the sales tax and pays a 30-cent-a-gallon excise tax instead (since July 1, 2025), left out here.
Hotel stays pay a 4% state lodgings tax (5% in the Mountain Lakes area counties) instead of the sales tax, plus local lodgings taxes, which are not counted here.
gaps: 9105 Fredonia is not in the 2024 Census place list; left out (its area takes the county rate)
9191 Pine Level is not in the 2024 Census place list; left out (its area takes the county rate)
9192 Kilpatrick is not in the 2024 Census place list; left out (its area takes the county rate)

City rates are for sales inside corporate limits. Most Alabama cities also tax sales in their police jurisdiction (usually half the city rate) outside city limits; those areas take the county rate here.
Southside (Calhoun/Etowah): ALDOR's code explanations put Calhoun levy 7408 inside its limits, but its own row cross-references 7008; the explanations are followed.

The Department of Revenue lists no separate grocery rate for one of the local levies in Avon town, Babbie town, Baileyton town, Benton town, Berlin town, Carolina town, Colony town, Dayton town, Deatsville town, Elmore County, Elmore town, Epes town, Goldville town, Gu-Win town, Holly Pond town, Horn Hill town, Lester town, Libertyville town, Maytown town, McMullen town, Memphis town, Nectar town, North Johns town, Oak Hill town, Onycha town, Paint Rock town, Petrey town, Pine Apple town, Pleasant Groves town, Pollard town, Providence town, Rosa town, Talladega Springs town, Twin town, Vredenburgh town, West Point town, Wetumpka city, so their general local rate is used for groceries; if one taxes groceries at a lower rate, their grocery rate here is too high.

32 cities lie in more than one county with different county levies, so their rate differs in each county part; a tract at least half in such a city takes the rate of its own county part: Altoona town, Arab city, Birmingham city, Calera city, Collinsville city, County Line town, Decatur city, Dothan city, Enterprise city, Garden City town, Helena city, Hoover city, Huntsville city, Lake View city, Leeds city, Madison city, McKenzie town, Millbrook city, Notasulga town, Piedmont city, Prattville city, Sand Rock town, Sardis City town, Taylor city, Trafford town, Trinity city, Vance city, Vestavia Hills city, Vincent town, Waverly town, Winfield city, Woodstock town.

Tax-abatement ("unabated") rates and amusement and other item-specific rates are not included. Of the restaurant and alcohol rates, Thomasville's 1% food service tax, Oxford's 7% alcohol rate and Jefferson County's 3% on beer and liquor and 6% on liquor served are counted; Columbiana's 4% on liquor and wine is noted on its page.

tiers.label: Alabama targeted and jumpstart counties
tiers.what: Under Code of Ala. §40-18-376.1(a) (Alabama Jobs Act, as amended 2019), every targeted or jumpstart county is an Enterprise Zone county-wide, so businesses there can qualify for Enterprise Zone tax credits or exemptions and for enhanced Alabama Jobs Act incentives.
tiers.none: Not a targeted or jumpstart county

programs: Tax increment financing districts are mapped for Mobile and Huntsville (its open districts; District 8, in Limestone County, isn't on the city's map), and Mobile's business improvement district as the city mapped it in 2022. Birmingham's only district layers date from 2018 and aren't current enough to use (its City Center business improvement district has no map), and Montgomery, Tuscaloosa and Hoover publish none. Main Street Alabama's 36 designated districts aren't shown: its district map marks each with a point on a statewide image, with no boundaries.

warn.text: Fairhope draws many visitors (its Mobile Bay waterfront and downtown), but it isn't flagged as a visitor economy: its seasonal homes (6.5%) and its 16 lodging places (0.7 per 1,000 residents) fall under the flag's cutoffs over the city as a whole, though one of its 4 census tracts is flagged on its own. Visitors' spending is part of its local sales, so its retention rates likely overstate how much of residents' own spending stays local.

Foley draws many visitors (the OWA theme park and its outlet mall, on the way to the Gulf beaches), but it isn't flagged as a visitor economy: its seasonal homes (3.3%) and its 20 lodging places (0.8 per 1,000 residents) fall under the flag's cutoffs. Visitors' spending is part of its local sales, so its retention rates likely overstate how much of residents' own spending stays local.

Guntersville draws many visitors (Lake Guntersville), but it isn't flagged as a visitor economy: its seasonal homes (3.6%) and its 17 lodging places (1.4 per 1,000 residents) fall under the flag's cutoffs over the city as a whole, though one of its 3 census tracts is flagged on its own. Visitors' spending is part of its local sales, so its retention rates likely overstate how much of residents' own spending stays local.

Fultondale may be flagged as a visitor economy only because of its hotels and motels along Interstate 65 (16 lodging places, 8.1 per 1,000 residents), serving travelers passing through, so read that flag with care.

Evergreen may be flagged as a visitor economy only because of its motels along Interstate 65 (6 lodging places, 3.6 per 1,000 residents), serving travelers passing through, so read that flag with care.

Redstone Arsenal is an Army post; its flag as a visitor economy rests on lodging for people on official travel there (7 lodging places, 6.1 per 1,000 residents), not on tourism, so read that flag with care.

Thomasville's flag as a visitor economy rests on its 9 lodging places (2.3 per 1,000 residents), just over the cutoff, in a small city that isn't a tourist destination; they likely serve work travel and people passing through more than tourists, so read that flag with care.
